definitions.text: Gives the degree of oxidation of an atom in terms of counting electrons. OS of an atom is the charge of this atom after ionic approximation of its heteronuclear bonds. The bond's electrons are assigned to its main atomic contributor. Homonuclear bonds are divided equally. In practical use, the ionic-approximation sign follows electronegativities. OS equals the charge of an atom after its heteronuclear bonds have been assigned to the more electronegative partner and homonuclear bonds have been divided equally.
